executive_summary: Security assessment of http://localhost:5000 identified 11 vulnerability finding(s), of which 10 were positively confirmed with proof-of-concept evidence. The overall risk posture is rated CRITICAL based on a highest CVSS base score of 9.8. Findings breakdown: 3 Critical, 3 High, 5 Medium, 0 Low. Immediate remediation is recommended for all Critical and High severity findings prior to any production deployment.

findings.title: User Enumeration via Login Error Messages
findings.description: Login error for non-existent user reveals account existence. Response: { "status": "fail", "message": "Username does not exist"}
findings.impact: Attackers can enumerate valid usernames by observing error message differences.
findings.proof_of_concept:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/users/v1/login \
  -d '{"username":"nonexistent_01df47","password":"x"}'
# Response reveals: user does not exist
remediation: Return a generic error message for all failed login attempts.
Use the same response for wrong username and wrong password.
Implement account lockout after N failed attempts.

findings.title: Broken Object Level Authorization — Cross-User Profile Read
findings.description: User 'bola_a_389cfd' (authenticated with their own JWT) successfully accessed User 'bola_b_389cfd's profile data by simply changing the username in the URL. The API does not verify that the requesting user owns the resource.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can read any other user's profile data, including potentially sensitive fields like email addresses and admin flags.
findings.proof_of_concept:
# Login as User A to get JWT
curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/users/v1/login -d '{"username":"bola_a_389cfd","password":"..."}'

# Use User A's JWT to access User B's data
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <JWT_A>' http://localhost:5000/users/v1/bola_b_389cfd
remediation: Verify that the authenticated user ID matches the requested resource owner ID.
Use the JWT sub/username claim to authorise resource access, not the URL parameter.
Implement object-level access control checks in every endpoint handler.
Return HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to access another user's resource.

findings.title: IDOR — Unauthorized Email Update on Another User's Account
findings.description: User 'bola_a_389cfd' successfully updated User 'bola_b_389cfd's email to 'hacked_62b257@evil.invalid'. This is an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability.
findings.impact: Account takeover: attacker changes victim's email and requests password reset.
remediation: Extract username from the validated JWT token, not the URL.
Verify the JWT subject matches the URL username before processing.
Implement resource ownership middleware for all user-scoped endpoints.

findings.title: IDOR — Unauthorized Password Change on Another User's Account
findings.description: User 'bola_a_389cfd' successfully changed User 'bola_b_389cfd's password without knowing the current password.
findings.impact: Complete account takeover — attacker locks victim out of their account.
remediation: Only allow users to change their own password (verify JWT subject == URL username).
Require current password confirmation before allowing password change.
Implement strong audit logging for all password change operations.

findings.title: User List Accessible Without Authentication
findings.description: The user listing endpoint returns data without any authentication. This exposes usernames and potentially other sensitive fields.
findings.impact: Enables user enumeration and reconnaissance for targeted attacks.
remediation: Require authentication for all user listing endpoints.
Restrict user listing to admin roles only.
Implement pagination and rate limiting on public endpoints.

findings.title: Potential SQL Injection — Email Update Endpoint (VAmPI Known Vulnerability)
findings.description: VAmPI's email update endpoint is documented as containing SQL injection. Automated error signatures were not detected (VAmPI may swallow errors), but manual testing with UNION-based payloads is recommended.
findings.impact: Potential full database access via SQL injection.

response_body.message: Please Provide a valid email address.
Please Provide a valid email address.

request_body.email: test' UNION SELECT username, password, 1 FROM users--@test.invalid

response_body.message: Please Provide a valid email address.

findings.proof_of_concept:
curl -X PUT http://localhost:5000/users/v1/inj_feaef731/email \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <JWT>' \
  -d '{"email":"' UNION SELECT username,password,1 FROM users--@x.com"}'
remediation: Use parameterised queries for all database interactions.
Validate and sanitise email format before query execution.

findings.title: Debug Endpoint Exposes Sensitive Data — /users/v1/_debug
findings.description: The /users/v1/_debug endpoint is accessible and returns data. Debug endpoints should never be exposed in any environment. Exposed sensitive fields: ['admin', 'password']
findings.impact: Debug endpoints can expose internal system details, all user records, and credentials.
remediation: Remove all debug/internal endpoints before deployment.
Use feature flags or environment-specific routing to disable debug routes.
If debug endpoints are needed, restrict to internal network only.
Implement proper access control: admin-only with IP whitelisting.

findings.title: Missing Security Headers in API Responses
findings.description: The following security headers are missing: ['x-content-type-options', 'x-frame-options', 'strict-transport-security', 'content-security-policy', 'x-xss-protection']
findings.impact: Increases attack surface for XSS, clickjacking, and MIME sniffing attacks.
remediation: Add missing headers: ['x-content-type-options', 'x-frame-options', 'strict-transport-security', 'content-security-policy', 'x-xss-protection']
Use a security headers middleware (e.g., flask-talisman).

findings.title: Mass Assignment — Admin Privilege Escalation via Registration
findings.description: The registration endpoint accepted the extra field(s) {"admin": true} and applied them to the user's account. The user 'mass_8877f51c' was registered with admin privileges by including {"admin": true} in the registration payload.
findings.impact: Any unauthenticated user can self-register as an administrator, gaining full administrative access to the application.

response_body.message: Successfully registered. Login to receive an auth token.

findings.proof_of_concept:
curl -X POST http://localhost:5000/users/v1/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"username": "hacker", "password": "pass", "email": "h@x.com", "admin": true}'
# Then login as 'hacker' — admin=true confirmed in profile
remediation: Use a whitelist of allowed registration fields: only username, email, password.
Never bind request body directly to the user model/ORM object.
Implement explicit field assignment instead of bulk update patterns.
Validate and reject any extra fields not in the allowed whitelist.
Use a dedicated registration DTO that excludes admin/role fields.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on Registration Endpoint — Account Creation Spam
findings.owasp_category: API4:2019 Lack of Resources & Rate Limiting
findings.description: Successfully registered 10 accounts in rapid succession without any rate limiting. All requests returned success status codes.
findings.impact: Attackers can create unlimited accounts (bot registration, spam, resource exhaustion of database and storage).
remediation: Implement IP-based rate limiting on registration (max 5/hour per IP).
Add email verification to prevent disposable email spam.
Implement CAPTCHA on registration.
Return HTTP 429 with Retry-After when limit exceeded.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on User Listing Endpoint
findings.owasp_category: API4:2019 Lack of Resources & Rate Limiting
findings.description: Sent 30 rapid GET requests to /users/v1 without 429. Unlimited scraping of user data is possible.
findings.impact: Enables bulk user enumeration and DoS via resource exhaustion.
remediation: Implement global API rate limiting (e.g., 100 requests/minute per IP).
Use a reverse proxy (nginx, Cloudflare) for rate limit enforcement.
Add pagination to prevent bulk data extraction in a single request.
